This is actually part of the issue with the FIFA rankings. The USA plays a *lot* of home matches, and FIFA doesn't even account for home field! So that biases our rating upwards except when games are actually played at home, which fortunately, they are just this once.

Well, at least you can't accuse me of playing favorites for our subscriber list (78% American).

FIFA's ranking for the US probably isn't right, I *will* say though that we tend to find a bigger home-field advantage than other models. MEX has a particularly big one.

We just launched PELE, our new soccer model! It is kind of insanely detailed. But we think you'll really like it and hope you'll check it out. Argentina *just* edges out Spain in the initial rankings. The US is ... much further down the list.

But at prediction markets, the swing after the VA decision is meaningful but measured. IDK, we'll see what our model says once we launch it. But you're not getting a great sense of the magnitude from reading this platform right now.
To be clear, I think the long-term situation is a bad equilibrium, and Democrats will have to retaliate further ahead of 2028 (and Republicans surely will, too).

It seems to me that people don't really have a good sense of how much a small number of House seats matter, given what will probably be a good overall night for Democrats in November, paired with high variance.

The idea that there needs to be a trade-off between minority representation and Democratic seats is mostly a myth. More in today's newsletter, including the introduction of two hypothetical states, Cumberland and Susquehanna.
